S56.01.needs: a Google account; a cloud account that can use connectors
S56.01.note: The ledger says the Gmail OAuth client pair is not yet in CONNECTOR_OAUTH_PROVIDERS_JSON, so Connect may fail or show Needs setup.
steps: Open Settings, tap the Cloud group, then tap Connectors.
Tap Gmail, then tap Connect and finish the Google sign-in.
Open a new chat, tap Add to chat, tap Connectors and turn Gmail on.
Type: Find emails from [a sender you know] about [a subject you know].
Compare: the reply lists matching messages from that mailbox, as Expected says.
S56.01.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Gmail > Connect, then Add to chat > Connectors (turn Gmail on) in a new chat

S56.02.needs: a Google account; a cloud account that can use connectors
S56.02.note: Same Gmail OAuth gap as S56.01: the ledger says the client pair is not yet configured.
steps: Connect Gmail as in S56.01 (Settings, Cloud, Connectors, Gmail, Connect).
Open a new chat, tap Add to chat, tap Connectors and turn Gmail on.
Type: Open the email from [a sender] about [a subject] and tell me what it says.
Compare: the reply shows the full text of that email or thread, not only a summary of the subject line.
S56.02.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Gmail > Connect, then Add to chat > Connectors (turn Gmail on) in a new chat

S56.03.needs: a Google account with Gmail; a cloud account that can use connectors
S56.03.note: The directory lists a create_draft tool for Gmail; the Gmail OAuth gap in S56.01 applies.
steps: Connect Gmail and turn it on in a new chat (as in S56.01).
Type: Draft a reply to [a sender] saying [a short message].
Check the reply: it says a draft was created.
Open Gmail in a browser or the Gmail app and look in Drafts for the new draft, as Expected says.
S56.03.where: Settings > Cloud > Connectors > Gmail > Connect, then Add to chat > Connectors (turn Gmail on) in a new chat
